given.part: An open loan's `dueOn` is before today (UTC)
given.why: Two loans due 2026-03-16 are set up, and the clock is moved to 2026-03-17, so both loans are overdue when the job runs.

given.part: it has no reminder recorded today
given.why: The job runs once on a fresh database, so neither loan has a reminder yet.

then.part: Asks the Notifications API to notify the loan's member
then.why: The fake's `sent` list must hold exactly the two reminders, each with the right memberId, loanId and dueOn, so a skipped call or a wrong memberId would fail.
The reminders table must hold exactly one row for each loan.
Each row's `sent_on` must be 2026-03-17, which is today, not the due date.
Recording before asking only shows when the API refuses. B3's test proves nothing is recorded for a refused loan, and that catches it.

given.part: An open loan already has a reminder recorded today
given.why: The job runs twice on the same day, so on the second run loan1 already has a reminder for today.
loan2 is overdue but is returned before the job runs.
The third loan is lent on 03-03, so it is due 03-17, which is today. That is the boundary case.

then.why: toMatchObject on an array also checks its length, so `sent` must hold exactly one entry, for loan1. Any extra send for the returned, not-yet-due or already-reminded loan would fail.

given.why: The fake refuses loan1 with a 503 reason.
B5 proves that a failed connection comes back as a `refused` delivery. B3's job handles every refused delivery the same way, and its test covers that.

then.why: The reminders table must equal exactly loan2's row, so any row for loan1 would fail.
The log entry's event name is matched exactly.
The log entry's level is matched exactly.
The fields must be exactly loan1's id plus the error.
The error must equal the exact reason the fake gave.

then.part: carries on with the other loans
then.why: loan1 is lent first and is due first, and loan2 must still be sent and recorded after loan1 is refused, so stopping the loop would fail.

given.part: The job has handled every overdue loan
given.why: Three loans are overdue, one of them refused, and the job runs over all of them.

then.why: The last log entry is matched exactly with toEqual.
The level is matched exactly.
`sent` must equal 2.
`failed` must equal 1.

given.why: Every test sends a fixed reminder through the real client.

then.why: The recorded request method must be POST, and the handler only matches POST.
The handler only matches NOTIFY_URL/notifications, and the recorded path must be exactly `/notifications`.
The content-type must be exactly application/json, and the body is parsed as JSON.
The body must contain memberId: member-1.

B5's body check uses expect.objectContaining and leaves out `template`, so a missing or wrong template still passes. Only the borrow-a-book system test (another spec's B3) pins it, and that is luck, not proof.
`data` must deep-equal { loanId: loan-1, dueOn: 2026-03-16 }, so renaming either key would fail.
202, 200 and 204 must each come back as `accepted`.
A 400 must come back as `refused`, which catches a client that only treats 5xx as refused.
A network error must come back as a `refused` delivery, not a thrown error.

then.part: with a reason naming the status
then.why: The reason must contain "400".

then.part: or saying the API was unreachable
then.why: The reason must contain "unreachable".
